title: 緊急時の国会議員任期延長　憲法改正で可能に　「賛成」36％
extracted_text: 毎日新聞の世論調査で、緊急事態の際に国会議員の任期を延長できるようにする憲法改正について尋ねたところ、賛成が36％で、反対の29％を上回った。ただ「わからない」も33％あった。 憲法改正を巡っては、自民党が2018年の第2次安倍晋三政権下で、「『自衛隊』の明記と『自衛の措置』の言及」「国会や内閣の緊急事態への対応を強化」など改憲4項目をまとめている。 調査は4月18、19日にスマートフォンを対象とした調査方式「dサーベイ」で実施した。NTTドコモのdポイントクラブ会員を対象としたアンケートサービスを使用し、全国の18歳以上約7700万人から調査対象者を無作為に抽出。1868人から有効回答を得た。【野原大輔】
translated_text: According to a Mainichi Shimbun public opinion survey, when asked about constitutional revision that would allow extending the terms of national legislators during emergencies, 36% were in favor, exceeding the 29% who were opposed. However, 33% also said they "don't know." Regarding constitutional revision, the Liberal Democratic Party compiled four revision items under the second Shinzo Abe administration in 2018, including "explicit mention of the 'Self-Defense Forces' and reference to 'self-defense measures'" and "strengthening responses to emergencies in the Diet and cabinet." The survey was conducted on April 18-19 using a smartphone-based method called "d-Survey." It used an questionnaire service targeting NTT Docomo's d Point Club members, randomly selecting respondents from approximately 77 million people aged 18 and older nationwide. Valid responses were obtained from 1,868 people.
title_en: Extending Lawmakers' Terms in Emergencies Through Constitutional Revision Supported by 36%
